newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Goh says no impropriety in poll conduct.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Goh says no impropriety in poll conduct.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong on Sunday denied opposition suggestions of violations of electoral protocol in one hotly-contested constituency during last week's general election, state television said.
He was responding to opposition complaints over potential violations in the Cheng San constituency.
The Worker's Party, which lost to the ruling People's Action Party (PAP) in that ward, alleged that three legal provisions might have been violated.
These included the presence of Goh and the two deputy prime ministers at polling centres and their meeting and talking to voters before they cast their ballots.
Goh said that though he visited different polling stations, he was never inside. "Nobody has ever accused the PAP of stuffing ballot boxes," he said.
Worker's Party chief Joshua Jeyaratnam told Reuters today his party would decide by Monday whether to lodge an official protest at the result in the multi-member Cheng San ward.
Jeyaratnam said the party was considering appealing to the United Nations commission on elections or submitting an election petition to the courts in Singapore.
Goh said that if Jeyaratnam felt he had evidence of "gross unfairness, it was within his right to file a petition for the courts to decide.
The ruling People's Action Party (PAP) won with 55 percent of the vote in Cheng San, and swept 81 out of 83 parliamentary seats in the general election on January 2.
